title: Child care growth plan and cultural grant deferral
subtitle: Also: chronic homelessness plan update, paramedic response times, Erb Street shelter delay, and Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group follow-up.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended a plan for new licensed child care spaces under the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care program {{vote:m6}}. It also asked for the Region to request an additional 997 spaces from the province. The committee added direction for the Regional Chair to advocate to Ontario for better wages and benefits for early childhood educators, and for capital funding for new and existing facilities. Staff said a workforce shortage and long waitlists could limit growth.

The committee deferred to the April 19 Council meeting the 2023 funding for two Key Cultural Institutions, the Kitchener Waterloo Symphony and THEMUSEUM {{vote:m3}}. It also deferred a proposed review of the grant program's eligibility criteria. Councillors wanted to see the full picture, including a request for operating funding for the Grand Philharmonic Choir, before deciding.

The committee also received updates, for information only, on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, the Erb Street shelter site, which is now expected to open at the end of April rather than April 15, and paramedic response times. It asked staff to add an Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group update to the tracking list. It then moved to a closed session.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended allocating new licensed child care spaces under the Canada-wide program, requesting 997 more spaces from the province, and having the Regional Chair advocate for fair wages for early childhood educators and for capital funding.
The committee deferred the 2023 funding allocations of $385,725 each for the Kitchener Waterloo Symphony and THEMUSEUM, and the related motions, to the April 19, 2023 Council meeting.
As part of the consent agenda, the committee recommended supporting a temporary public art installation along the ION corridor and GRT bus route with up to $20,000 from the Public Art Reserve.

debate: On the cultural grants, one councillor noted that both funded institutions are in Kitchener and asked about other parts of the region. Staff said the criteria, such as an operating budget of about a million dollars and use of municipally owned buildings, exclude smaller groups like the Fashion History Museum. Staff said there is no geographic rule.

A delegate who chairs the Grand Philharmonic Choir supported the two recommended grants but asked the Region to continue its $32,000 operating funding. The delegate said the choir would have to cut programs without it and objected to a funding model based on visitors from outside the region.

Staff said the Region never intended to cut the choir's funding. They said a separate grant program, funded by the municipal accommodation tax, is coming to Council in May. Some councillors said past council-by-council funding lacked a formal process. Others said the split into two policies left them confused about the full package and asked to see everything together.

On child care, staff said the workforce crisis could stop growth, since early childhood educators earn little more than staff in roles that need only high school. Councillors asked about capital costs, since the maximum capital funding is about $350,000 per large program. They also asked about the waitlist and about reusing surplus Regional properties. The Chief Administrative Officer said a report on properties is coming to Council.

On the homelessness plan, some councillors said "ending" chronic homelessness may be unrealistic and may leave out hidden homelessness. They also asked for local municipalities to be added to the co-creator list. Staff called the plan aspirational and said shelter work would continue in the meantime.
